title: Flexible pin selector compatibility and resolution algorithm for model references
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Goal: Define a clear, backward-compatible resolution algorithm and SDK surface for pinning models by tag, semver (including ranges), and commit/digest, while publishing and validating performance profiles during onboarding. Deliverables: 1) a spec for resolver precedence and tie-breaking, 2) SDK model-ref types and example usages, 3) runtime validation and compatibility checks for performance profiles (KV cache format, quantization profile, kernel constraints), 4) caching/TTL semantics and observable traces for resolution decisions, 5) migration guidance for existing pinned refs. Background: Users currently expect deterministic pinning semantics when they pin a model in the API or SDK. We must support three primary pin forms: tag (e.g., "@stable", "@prod-2026-03"), semver (exact: "1.3.2", range: "^1.3.0"), and immutable commit/digest (e.g., "@sha256:abcd..."). We must also surface and publish a performance profile tied to a model version so upstream consumers can make cost/latency tradeoffs. Resolution algorithm (draft): 1) If request includes an immutable digest/commit -> resolve to that exact artifact; verify signed manifest and published perf-profile. 2) Else if request includes an explicit commit-ish (short commit string) -> attempt exact lookup; if ambiguous return error with candidates and suggestion to use digest. 3) Else if request includes semver exact (e.g., "1.3.2") -> resolve exact semver tag if present, else error. 4) Else if request includes semver range (e.g., "^1.3.0") -> select highest compatible release that: a) satisfies range, b) has compatible perf-profile for caller runtime (GPU arch, quantization support), c) prefers release with published stability flag true. If multiple candidates equal, choose the most recent published. 5) Else if request includes tag name -> resolve to tag pointer; tags are mutable and resolution must return the current digest with its perf-profile and last-updated metadata. 6) Else when user asks for "latest" or unspecified -> use default routing policy (customer-specific default -> region default -> org-level fallback). Fallbacks: Provide policy options: fail-fast on missing compatibility vs soft-fallback to nearest compatible lower-version variant. Publishable performance profile contract: Every model artifact must include a normalized perf-profile JSON: fields (p99_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec, kv_cache_version, quantization_profiles, supported_kernels, memory_peak_mb, verified_on_hardware_tags). Profile publishing rules: - On model onboarding, registry must validate presence and schema. - Runtime must check kv_cache_version and quantization_profiles compatibility; if mismatch and policy==strict then fail resolution. SDK surface: - ModelRef union: {digest: string} | {commit: string} | {semver: string | range} | {tag: string} - New API parameter: "resolve_policy": "strict" | "allow_fallback" | "prefer_stable" with clear semantics. - Add resolution metadata to response headers and SDK response object: resolved_digest, resolved_version, resolution_path, perf_profile_snapshot_url. Caching: - Resolver cache keyed by (requested_ref, project, region, resolve_policy). TTL default 120s, invalidated on tag mutation events (webhook). - SDK should expose a way to force-refresh. Observability: - Emit a trace/span for resolution including start/end, chosen_reason, candidate_count, perf_profile_hash. - Add dashboard in Console: per-route resolution failures, avg resolution latency, fallback rate. Trade-offs considered: - Simplicity vs power: supporting semver ranges gives flexibility but complicates caching and determinism. Recommend semver ranges be allowed for internal/service-to-service calls only by default; default SDK helper should encourage exact or digest pins for user-facing code. - Mutable tags are convenient but dangerous for reproducibility; strongly recommend showing resolved_digest in logs. - Strict compatibility checks reduce silent runtime regressions, but may block quick rollouts; support allow_fallback to fall back to lower-fidelity variants. Migration notes: - Existing pinned-by-tag references will continue to resolve to current digest; update SDK docs to show resolved_digest in logs. - Provide a small migration tool to enumerate pinned refs in customer projects and expand tags into the digest + perf-profile snapshot for archival. Next steps: - Align on final resolver precedence and publish design doc (link in comments). - Implement SDK types and unit tests (PR drafted). - Runtime changes: manifest validation and compatibility checks. - QA: e2e with Dedicated and Private deployments to validate policy behaviors.
comments: 2026-02-26 Marco Ruiz: Initial proposal posted to #model-infra. Key open question: should semver ranges be resolved deterministically across regions? I propose choosing the highest compatible published release globally and then checking region availability; will add to spec.

2026-03-02 Priya Nandakumar: Design review notes - prefer explicit 'prefer_stable' policy instead of 'prefer_recent' to reduce surprises for SREs. Also request an example SDK snippet for the Node/Python SDKs.

2026-03-05 Samira Patel: Security review: ensure digest resolution verifies artifact signature and that perf-profile URLs respect org ACLs. Marked security_review_required=false for now but gating signature verification into runtime change; will re-open if KMS/HSM integration impacted.

2026-03-07 Alex Chen: Engineering feasibility check: runtime needs ability to reject resolution if kv_cache_version mismatches; that requires a small manifest field and a KV schema bump. Blocking PR for runtime is linked below.

2026-03-09 Marco Ruiz: Linked artifacts - design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Pinning+Resolution+Spec, PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8342, SDK PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2190

2026-03-12 Priya Nandakumar: Added unit test matrix for semver ranges and tag mutations (cases: overlapping releases, missing perf-profiles, incompatible kernels). Tests added in SDK PR but runtime hooks pending.
